critical_breaks.title: Runtime silently auto-updates after preflight
API schema drift changes the meaning of an authorized action
External write succeeds but response times out, enabling duplicate effects
Stale tests remain green after their source or runtime basis changes
All tests pass while an Owner requirement is missing
Stale, revoked, or wrong-target authorization envelope is accepted
Workers continue under superseded Owner intent
Disk-full checkpoint failure loses the record of an external effect
Removed or replaced worktree is mistaken for the owned checkout
Duplicate automation resume performs the same effect twice
Two agents resume the same state without enforced mutation ownership
Technical remediation silently expands admitted scope
An available alternative is chosen without authority or requirement equivalence
Architecture or security decision is hidden inside implementation
Git success overrides a failed or unverified external outcome
Review remediation is marked complete without tests or valid rereview
Empty applicable-predicate set closes unfinished work
Required live proof is declared not applicable merely to close
Replanning erases a blocked acceptance predicate
Fabricated evidence or green flags are accepted as proof
Worker self-report substitutes for independent observation
Generic push permission publishes to the wrong branch or repository
Broad staging commits unrelated dirty work
A stale or shared path enables overwriting another worktree
An unsafe or unknown-outcome operation is retried
REJECT or technical failure does not invalidate previous green predicates
READ_ONLY Git invocation executes an effectful ambient helper
Duplicate requirement ID shadows an accepted hard constraint

high_risk_breaks.title: Unavailable model causes false escalation or unauthorized substitution
Runtime version mismatch is mistaken for an executable capability
Intermittent network creates unbounded or unsafe retries
Login expiry loses principal binding or effect progress
2FA challenge is misclassified as technical repair
Successful Git push with client failure is not reconciled
Wrong reviewer verdict is treated as authoritative
Reviewer and implementer disagree without bounded adjudication
Badly scoped current increment traps or silently shrinks the work
Lost chat context causes invented intent or unsafe replay
Execution-window end suppresses an honest stop or creates a false resume promise
Locked state database causes endless waiting or persistence bypass
Upstream advance invalidates grounding and verification
Deleted evidence references leave unsupported green claims
Disappearing dependency triggers endless research or a material unauthorized replacement
Universal alternatives-exhausted proof prevents termination
Difficult reasoning is disguised as OWNER_BLOCKER
Autonomous repair repeats without persistent progress budgets
Agent returns early without invoking an optional gate
Stale authored STATUS overrides current Git observations
Resume key presence hides null or contradictory state
Evaluator exit code zero is mistaken for completed delivery
Malformed state crashes the evaluator without a structured verdict
Matching fingerprints admit a package containing failed S3 gates

minimum_required_defenses.title: Strict action and response gate at the actual integration boundary
Versioned obligations preserved through admission, applicability, and replanning
Effective scoped authorization with action-time revocation and intent-generation checks
Capability freshness and relevant runtime identity checked at the point of use
Durable journal, validated checkpoints, and failure-aware reconciliation
Single active writer with atomic claims and enforced fencing where takeover exists
Durable effect intent, stable operation identity, supported deduplication, and reconciliation
Owned Git worktree and staging scope, explicit publication target, remote ref verification
Protected observed evidence, frozen review basis, behavioral coverage, and predicate invalidation
Persistent progress budgets, finite eligible alternatives, and honest operational stops
Narrow effect mediation and an enforced rather than declarative read-only boundary

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: Product outcome, capability, increment, and task remain distinct
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Sound documented boundary, not proof that every increment is correctly scoped

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: Capability availability is separate from authority
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Sound documented distinction; general action-time enforcement is still needed

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: Recognized Owner-only, external-permission, and execution-window events are distinguished
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Reproduced for the recognized event classes; free-text and semantic classification remain limited

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: A declared required predicate that is false blocks final completion
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Positive control passed; caller-controlled applicability remains vulnerable

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: Selected hard-reference, superseded-decision, and unequal-baseline checks
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Positive controls passed; these do not establish semantic coverage or current external authority

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: Context freshness validator reads actual selected files and Git
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Implementation inspected, not newly executed in this audit; not a general live-capability freshness mechanism

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: S3c checks declared authorization scope and evidence basis
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Implementation inspected; declared provenance is not authenticated general execution authority

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: S3d has a real bounded runner with explicit execution, digest, timeout, and receipt-path checks
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Implementation inspected and selected components probed; not a general orchestrator or a proven no-effect sandbox

design_elements_that_survived_attack.element: Implementation claims, worker reports, acceptance, and platform limits are distinguished in policy
design_elements_that_survived_attack.status: Useful contract preserved; original goal honestly scoped a simulator rather than a general orchestration runtime

audit_scope.interpretation: Scenario counts are not counts of independent code defects or live exploits. Per-scenario reproduced, inspected, and proposed evidence classifications are in FAILURE_MATRIX.md.
limits: Inspected pinned active workflow, adapter, validators, simulator, bounded runner, and relevant goal evidence; not an exhaustive audit of every historical file.
No live Codex end-to-end session or production failure injection was performed.
No payments, credential operations, duplicate external messages, production mutations, or owner-worktree destruction were performed.
No source AI OS or NovaStory files were changed. Defenses are proposals, not implemented fixes.

verification.method: Selected connector-returned source copies were verified against Git blob SHA before isolated local execution.
verification.negative_probe_meaning: The unwanted component behavior was reproduced; this is not a safety pass or proof of a complete live exploit.
